### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d70e94ae1db083f2ef136e0a65597b2de09fd35f`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d70e94ae1db083f2ef136e0a65597b2de09fd35f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cfc749f962dd3e83d40cb25b328fafc25bdfa5eb` — the merge of head `91a1d307f2d6a9a12d1c482682d139efe7a6f3b7` into base `d70e94ae1db083f2ef136e0a65597b2de09fd35f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cfc749f962dd3e83d40cb25b328fafc25bdfa5eb && git checkout cfc749f962dd3e83d40cb25b328fafc25bdfa5eb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d70e94ae1db083f2ef136e0a65597b2de09fd35f 91a1d307f2d6a9a12d1c482682d139efe7a6f3b7 && git checkout -B drift-repro d70e94ae1db083f2ef136e0a65597b2de09fd35f && git merge --no-ff 91a1d307f2d6a9a12d1c482682d139efe7a6f3b7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d70e94ae1db083f2ef136e0a65597b2de09fd35f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d70e94ae1db083f2ef136e0a65597b2de09fd35f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `69182e333b046d67525ea9494ebb8d55ebf3c85d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-objects.test.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-security-seal.test.ts` + `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (the body seam `registerMetadataCollections`, `resolveMetadataItemName`, `permissionSetOwnerRegistrationRefusal`, `stampPackage`), `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (`registerItem`, `collectManifestBoundActions`), `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` (`unclaimedTopLevel`, `artifactItemSlot`, `ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE`, `registerUnclaimedTopLevel`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (`isSealedManagedItem`, `isArtifactBacked`), `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts` (the security and picklist rows), `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ui/assembled-views.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ui/view-container-object.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` (the config door's residual half), `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-lock.ts`, `.changeset/28093-residual-top-level-items-register.md`, `docs/adr/0130-release-artifact-as-co-ownership-boundary.md` D4.

Inputs: card #28093 (body; triage 6523369904; claim 6523676782; os-dev report 6525127678), PR #28153 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's check-runs, and the maintainer-only mechanism report (read; nothing from it is quoted here). Read-only: the tree was judged, not run.

Check-runs at 2026-10-30T14:42Z: every gate-carrying context that has concluded is `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test Core` shards 1-4 and 6-8); `Test Core (5/8)` is still `in_progress`, so the aggregate `Test Core` context has not reported. The verdict below is on the diff; the landing still waits on that shard.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **Residual items of every registry type now reach the engine registry** — right. `unclaimedTopLevel` lists 28 types (`ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE`); the head registers all of them except `object` (own path, unchanged), `picklist` (deliberately metadata-only, see ③) and `object_extension` (never listed). Each is registered after every body, under the residual rule's `ownerId`/`ownerVersion` (the stack's `manifest.id`/`version`, with the `id`/`version` top-level fallback the rule itself uses), stamped on a shallow copy, through `registry.registerItem(type, …, 'name', ownerId)` — the verb the body seam uses. The artifact's own entries are left as they arrived (pinned).
2. **The managed-content seal now covers a residual security rule** — right, and it is the card's security half. `isSealedManagedItem` is `isArtifactBacked && !registryAllowsOverlay`, and `isArtifactBacked` is a registry lookup, so a residual item of a non-overlayable type is sealed exactly when it is in the registry. On `main` a residual `permission` or `position` (the two security types with `allowRuntimeCreate: true`) fell to the runtime-create tier at the save door; on the head it is refused `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. The other four security types fail closed on both trees (`NOT_CREATABLE`). Stated at rule level only.
3. **New boot-time refusals for residual items** — right, and not a narrowing. A residual permission set whose body `packageId` names another package (ADR-0086 D3), an off-contract action (`parsePackageAction`), a divergent view container (`viewContainerNameRefusal`) and a queue or assignment rule on a composition without an ownership-queue service (ADR-0142 D1, `assertOwnershipQueueServicePresent` reads `registry.listItems('queue'|'assignment_rule')`) now refuse the boot where the same item in a package body already refused it. Is any composed stack that boots on `main` now refused? Yes, in exactly those four classes — and in each the item was not accepted on `main` either: it was dropped from the registry in silence, and a queue so dropped was inert. The divergent container was already refused on `main` by the config boot's metadata door (`registerUnclaimedTopLevel` throws the same refusal). The published accept set (`packages/spec`) is untouched; what changed is that the runtime now enforces what the contract already declared (Prime Directive #10, declared = enforced), which is the triage ruling's second arm ("refuse it loudly at boot"). So `yes (widening)` covers it and no `(narrowing)` arm is owed.
4. **The late-artifact bound-action target check now judges the residual's actions with the bodies'** — right. `collectManifestBoundActions({ actions }, ownerId)` tolerates an empty list and an undefined owner.
5. **The `arrived` set for collision reporting falls back to the residual items' owner when the residual has no objects** — right.
6. **No public export, route, schema or spec surface changes.** `packages/spec` is untouched; the PR body's "nothing an author can write changes" holds in the tree.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28093-residual-top-level-items-register.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` `patch`; body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, both line-initial, matching the PR body. The only published package the diff moves is `@objectstack/objectql`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` against `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`: `yes` with the `(widening)` arm is the legal spelling of "the accept set widens"; the arm is the value said out loud. Right — declared residual items that were refused no reader of the registry now register (①.1). The new refusals (①.3) are enforcement of the existing contract, not a narrowing of it, so `yes (narrowing)` is not owed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — right: no key, value, type or default an author writes changes.
- Level per AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: the level follows the kind alone; `none` takes `patch`. A widening with `Metadata-protocol: none` ships `patch`. Right. (The older "both take at least minor" sentence in `clause2-line.mjs`'s arm docblock is superseded by ruling A in the same file's header, which AGENTS.md step 3 states.)
- Title carries no `!`; no BREAKING banner is owed; no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` in the os-dev report — none to answer.
- Dev flag (acceptance note + `out_of_scope_findings`, "carrier: none"): **picklists stay metadata-only.** Answered in part: the reason holds (the residual objects rule already judges an object whose field names a residual-only picklist as "listed and not served", pinned on `main`; registering residual picklists in this PR would move that ruled line), and the seal has no stake in it (`picklist` is `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false, allowRuntimeCreate: false`, so a save over one is refused on both trees). Not answered: a residual picklist that no object references is still the one listed type that is neither registered in the engine nor refused, and its absence is loud only through an object that names it — "carrier: none" leaves the triage's "no type is dropped silently" half-answered for one type. **Escalated as should-fix #3** below: file the follow-up card; the carrier is the card, not "none".
- The PR body says the head is 17 commits behind `origin/main` and none touches the changed files; not re-measured here (read-only), the merge is the queue's.
- Governed surfaces: none in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). Hot file `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` untouched, as the claim required; the price is should-fix #2.
- Ablation and run figures in the PR body (41/45 red on `main`, 60/60 green, 9647 passed) are the dev's; this record relies on the check-runs and the read, not on them.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`** — holds, with two should-fixes. Against the body seam it cites (`registerMetadataCollections`): the same `registerItem` verb, the same owner stamp (`applyProtection` on a copy; the seam's `stampPackage` mutates in place, so the copy is the right call), the same view container derivation and expansion (`deriveViewContainerObject`, `expandViewContainer`), the same divergent-name judge, the same permission owner judge, and the seam's post-registration judges (`parsePackageAction`, the security-catalog name conflict, the page refusals) all run inside `registerItem` with `ownerId` as `packageId`, so they apply to a residual item unchanged. Break attempts:
- *Double registration of body-declared items*: `unclaimedTopLevel` filters on the slot every body claims (a container on its object and each view it expands into; every other item on its name), so a top-level item a body repeats is never in the residual; the body-repeat pin holds 11 types at the body's owner, once. Holds.
- *Picklists and objects keeping their own path*: `RESIDUAL_TYPES_WITH_OWN_PATH` excludes them from `unclaimedTopLevelItems`; `unclaimedTopLevelObjects` is unchanged in behaviour (now fed the one shared answer — the #28091 should-fix closed). Holds.
- *Ownership under the stack's manifest id and version*: owner read from the one rule's answer, version stamped before `registerItem`; pinned per type and all-at-once. Holds.
- *Ordering against the automation and security plugins' `start()`*: the manifest service registers in the registering plugin's `init()` (declared dependency on the engine), before any `start()`; service-automation's boot pull and plugin-security's `classifyPackagedPermissionSet` (request-time, registry first) both read after. Later `manifest.register` calls (install, rehydrate) take the late-artifact path the diff extends. Holds.
- *A stack with no residual items*: `unclaimedTopLevelItems` answers `undefined`, the call is skipped, the "registered nothing" branch keeps its three-way condition; CONTROL pin holds. A stack without `packages[]` has no residual by the rule. Holds.
- *AppPlugin as a second registrar*: for a `packages[]` bundle the config door registers the residual into the metadata service only and leaves the engine to the `manifest` service, so no second engine registration. Holds.
- **Should-fix #1 — the residual `view` branch is wider than the body seam's for a non-container entry.** The residual rule lists a `views:` entry that is not an aggregated container by its `name`, or by `deriveViewContainerObject` when it has none. The head then registers it through the generic `registerItem('view', stamp(item), 'name', …)`. The body seam, for the same entry, (a) mints `name: itemName` when the item has none, and (b) refuses a non-container-shaped entry (`isViewContainerShaped`, 422 `INVALID_METADATA`, the #5320 tighten). On the head: a residual ViewItem or flattened overlay registers where a body's is refused; and a residual container-shaped entry with `object` but no `name` and no `list`/`form` registers under the key the string `undefined`, not under its object — a slot the residual rule claimed under one key and the engine filed under another. Reachable through `strict: false` and programmatic stacks only (the class the PR body already names), not a security type, so should-fix: give the non-container branch the body seam's two lines (mint the name from the slot, refuse the non-container shape with the seam's envelope). The docblock's "refuse alike" then becomes true for views.
- **Should-fix #2 — the permission refusal envelope is a copy.** `permissionSetOwnerRegistrationRefusal` in `engine.ts` is module-private, so the head rebuilds its `VALIDATION_ERROR`/400/`issues[]` envelope inline. The judge is shared (one comparison, as ADR-0086 D3 requires); the envelope is now two copies that can drift. Export the helper (one word in the hot file) or move it beside `viewContainerNameRefusal`, and call it from both doors.

**`packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-objects.test.ts`** — holds. The new describe pins, per type and all at once, registration under the stack's id and version; the artifact's own entries unstamped; container registration under its object with expansion; the divergent-name refusal in the body seam's words (asserted by calling the one judge, not a copied string); queues and assignment rules registering with the service and refusing without it (the ADR-0142 prescription asserted by regex); the foreign-`packageId` permission refusal; body-repeat (11 types, owner and single registration); CONTROL. Fixtures: body items are schema-valid where the body is strictly parsed; residual generic items are `{name,label}` only and register because `registerItem` logs and tolerates a schema miss — so those pins hold keying and ownership, not schema validity, which is the body seam's behaviour too. Nothing pins the non-container view case of should-fix #1.

**`packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-security-seal.test.ts`** — holds, and it is the security pin asked for. Does it exercise the save door's sealed-managed check for every `security` type with `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false`? Yes: the population is read from `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` (six types today, each with a fixture, and a type that joins without one fails the first case by name); each boots through the `manifest` service, is read back by `getArtifactItem` under the stack's id, and a `saveMetaItem` over it on a real protocol over a memory driver is asserted `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` with zero stored rows — the same door `isSealedManagedItem` guards, through `isArtifactBacked`. The by-name read after the refusal serves the declared set. The CONTROL (an undeclared `position` saves) shows the refusal is the seal and not a blanket `NOT_CREATABLE`; for the four `allowRuntimeCreate: false` types the pin distinguishes `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` from the `NOT_CREATABLE` they gave on `main`, so it is red there for every member. One limit, not a finding: it holds the engine half alone (no `MetadataPlugin` composed), which is the half the fix moves.

**Should-fix #3 (card-level, from ③):** file the follow-up card for residual picklists so the one type this PR neither registers nor refuses has a carrier.

No must-fix. No fail-open finding at rule level beyond the one the card names and the head closes.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `91a1d307f2d6a9a12d1c482682d139efe7a6f3b7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-objects.test.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-security-seal.test.ts` + `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (the body seam `registerMetadataCollections`, `resolveMetadataItemName`), `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (`registerItem`), `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` (`unclaimedTopLevel`, `artifactItemSlot`), `packages/spec/src/ui/assembled-views.zod.ts` (`isViewContainerShaped`), `packages/spec/src/ui/view-container-object.ts`, `.changeset/28093-residual-top-level-items-register.md`. The rest of the first record's scope was re-read only where this delta touches it.

This record supersedes 6525505738 (head `69182e33`), a PASS with three should-fixes. Delta reviewed: `69182e333b046d67525ea9494ebb8d55ebf3c85d..91a1d307f2d6a9a12d1c482682d139efe7a6f3b7` — the merge `0ca4c535` and the fix `91a1d307` — with the merge's effect on `plugin.ts` judged through the net diff against `main`, not the merge commit's own diff. Inputs as before (card #28093 with every comment; PR body, file list, net diff; the head's check-runs; the maintainer-only report, read and not quoted). Read-only.

Check-runs at 2026-10-30T15:08Z: concluded and `success`: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test UI`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`. Still `in_progress`: `Build Core`, `Test Core` (all 8 shards), `Type Check` (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), `Live E2E UI`, and the remaining `Lint ·` legs — so `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` and `Live E2E UI` have not reported on this head. The verdict below is on the diff; the landing waits on those.

### ① Derived judgments

The merge, judged by the tree:
1. **`0ca4c535` is a plain merge.** Its tree is byte-identical to the automatic merge of its two parents (`69182e33` and `48c77807`, the `origin/main` it took in); nothing was resolved by hand. Between the first record's base (`27e0bd58`) and the merge-base (`48c77807`) no commit on `main` touched `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `engine.ts`, `registry.ts` or `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`; `6a648ac2` (the engine's empty-search-fields refusal, `engine.ts` only) was already in `27e0bd58` and so already under the first record. The net `plugin.ts` delta against `main` after the merge differs from the one before it by exactly the fix commit's lines (interdiff read), and the net file list is still the same four files. Nothing the first record judged in ① moves; the first record's ①.1–①.6 stand.

The fix, judged by the tree (`registerUnclaimedTopLevelItems`, the generic branch after the container branch and the permission judge):
2. **A residual non-container `view` entry with no `name` is filed under its slot** — right. `name = item.name || deriveViewContainerObject(item)` for `type === 'view'`, `toRegister = { ...item, name }` when it differs: the key the residual rule claimed (`artifactItemSlot`'s object fallback) and the key the engine files under now agree, and it is the body seam's own derivation order (`resolveMetadataItemName`: own `name` first, then the object). The copy keeps the artifact's own entry unstamped and unnamed (pinned). For a non-`view` item `name` is `item.name`, which the residual rule guarantees, so the generic branch is unchanged for every other type.
3. **A residual `views:` entry that is not container-shaped is refused** — right. `isViewContainerShaped(toRegister)` — the same classifier, judged on the same name-minted item as the seam judges it — and the seam's `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 / `httpStatus` envelope with the seam's words, with `manifest` as the source label (the word the residual rule itself uses for the config door). A residual ViewItem or flattened overlay now refuses the boot where a body's did; the #5320 "runtime wider than schema" hole the first record found is closed for the residual. Reachable only through `strict: false` and programmatic stacks, as before; a new boot refusal in the same class as the four the first record judged — enforcement of what the body seam already declared, not a narrowing.
4. **Accept-set direction unchanged.** Still `yes (widening)` with no `(narrowing)` arm owed: the fix removes a leniency the head itself had introduced over `main` (on `main` the residual was not registered at all), so against `main` nothing that booted is newly refused by it except that strict-refused class.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: still `@objectstack/objectql` `patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the changeset and the PR body (head `91a1d307` is the PR's head). The body gained the one clause naming the 422 refusal of a non-container `views:` entry — right, that is what the diff now does.
- Level per AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 unchanged: the kind is `none`, so `patch`. Right. `packages/spec` untouched; no public surface moves; no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 disposition owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- First record should-fix #1 (view branch wider than the body seam): **taken** in `91a1d307`, both halves (name minting and shape refusal), with three pins — the nameless container-shaped entry filed under its object, and the two non-container shapes (flattened overlay without `name`; ViewItem) refused with the seam's code, status and words. Closed.
- First record should-fix #2 (permission refusal envelope copied from the module-private `permissionSetOwnerRegistrationRefusal`): **filed** as #28160 (open, `finding`, rides the `engine.ts` queue). The fix adds a second copied text — the 422 message of the seam's `views:` tighten, now in `engine.ts` and `plugin.ts` — for the same reason (the seam lives in the hot file) and the docblock says so. **Should-fix, carried:** #28160's scope should name both copies (the envelope helper and the `views:` message) so one `engine.ts` edit exports or relocates both; a card that closes the first and leaves the second would leave a drift seam the pins only partly hold (the test asserts the message text, so a drift is caught in words at least). No new card owed.
- First record should-fix #3 (residual picklist neither registered nor refused): **filed** as #28159 (open, p2, `pm:queue`). Carried; nothing further owed on this PR.
- `open_questions` of the os-dev report: none. No dev flag added in the delta.
- Governed surfaces: none in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green on this head). PR still draft, awaiting this record and green checks.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`** — holds. The delta's one method now runs, for a `view`: the container branch (name judge, file under object, expand) or, for everything else, name-from-slot then the container-shape judge then `registerItem`; the body seam runs name judge, name-from-slot, shape judge, `registerItem`, then expansion — the same judges on the same inputs, in an order that only differs in where the container branch returns. Break attempts on the fix: a residual entry with `name: ''` and no `object` has no slot, so the residual rule never lists it (the seam's `warn` and skip is therefore unreachable here, not missing); a non-`view` item with no `name` is likewise never listed; a `view` with a `name` that is also container-shaped but not an aggregated container (`{ name, object }`) is filed under its own name as the seam files it; the three first-record should-fix shapes now each take the seam's branch. The permission branch, stamping, ownership and ordering judgments of the first record are unchanged by the delta (interdiff). The merge brings no change to this file.
